content.thinking:
I need to set up the imports for the builder, paint, path, math, and texture modules, then structure the file to export a default function returning the builder's root object, following the convention where reading the root bakes the geometry. I'm planning to model an elephant with this setup.

I'm sketching the proportions: shoulder height around 3.2m, body length about 5m facing the +Z axis. I'll build the body as a swept ellipse along a curved spine path, legs as seven-sided rod pillars from hip to ground with slightly flattened feet, positioning front legs further forward and back legs further back to match the body curve.

Now I'm shaping the head and ears -- a scaled sphere for the skull with a forehead dome, and large flat extruded ear outlines positioned on the sides of the head, angled slightly to feel natural.

Still building trunk geometry...

Now I'm thinking through tusks: curved spikes sweeping outward from the head, forward and down then up with tapering ivory radius, anchored near the base of the trunk.

Then I'm positioning the eyes: small spheres computed from the head sphere's surface geometry so they sit naturally at the front, with white-brown coloring and tiny brow bumps added above.

For the tail, I'm sweeping a thin tapering capsule curving down and back, finishing with a dark tufted brush at the tip.

I still need to blend the neck-to-head connection with a loft or shoulder hump, add forehead and jaw/cheek bumps, and apply a mottled paint texture across the whole body with nested countershading for the belly.

Writing dust gradient paint...

Checking the cross product directions for the ear normal gives inconsistent forward/backward results across the two sides, so I'll abandon the offset inner-ear idea and instead make the ear a single thicker extrude, choosing its paint based on the surface normal direction.

For coloring, I'll define an elliptical region in the surface coordinates to mark the pinkish inner-ear area versus the grey skin tone, blending the two colors with a mix function and defaulting to the skin paint elsewhere. Then I'll position the ear on the head using the surface parameters.

Still working out ear placement...

Writing leg and foot geometry...

Still building geometry details...
